notes.summary: This chapter covers percentages and percentage change, successive changes, ratio and proportion, and averages including weighted and replacement averages. RRB NTPC and Group D ask 3-5 short questions here, and knowing fraction equivalents and a few shortcuts makes most of them one-line sums.
keyPoints: Successive change: net % = a + b + (a × b)/100, with a minus sign for a decrease. +20% then −20% gives 20 − 20 − 4 = −4%.
If A is r% more than B, then B is [r/(100 + r)] × 100 % less than A. 25% more means 20% less.
Growth at different yearly rates: final = P × (1 + r1/100) × (1 + r2/100). 20,000 at 10% then 5% → 23,100.
Combining ratios: A : B = 2 : 3 and B : C = 4 : 5 → make B the same (12) → A : B : C = 8 : 12 : 15.
Mean proportional of a and b = √(ab) (9 and 16 → 12); fourth proportional to a, b, c = (b × c)/a.
Replacement: if replacing one item changes the average of n items by d, new item = old item ± n × d.
Weighted average = (n1 × a1 + n2 × a2) ÷ (n1 + n2); it equals the simple mean of a1 and a2 only when n1 = n2.
Average of consecutive numbers (or any evenly spaced list) = middle term = (first + last) ÷ 2.
Coin problems: change the ratio of numbers of coins into a ratio of values before dividing the total amount.
traps: Adding successive percentages directly (+20% and −20% is not 0%).
Calculating percentage change on the new value instead of the original value.
Taking the simple mean of two group averages when the group sizes are different.
In election questions, applying the winner's percentage to total votes when it is given on valid votes.
In coin questions, dividing the rupee total in the ratio of number of coins instead of their values.
notes.examTip: When a base value is not given, assume 100 (₹100 income, 100 votes, ₹100 price) — most percentage word problems then become simple subtraction.

questions.text: Section A has 30 students with an average score of 60, and Section B has 20 students with an average score of 70. What is the average score of all 50 students together?
questions.explanation:
Total of Section A = 30 × 60 = 1800; total of Section B = 20 × 70 = 1400.
Combined total = 3200 for 50 students.
Average = 3200 ÷ 50 = 64. (65 is the simple mean of the two averages and ignores the different class sizes.) Answer: 64.

questions.text: The average of five consecutive odd numbers is 27. What is the largest of these numbers?
questions.explanation:
For evenly spaced numbers, the average is the middle (3rd) number, so the middle number is 27.
The five numbers are 23, 25, 27, 29, 31.
Largest = 31. Answer: 31.

questions.text: What is the mean proportional between 9 and 16?
questions.explanation:
Mean proportional between a and b = √(a × b).
√(9 × 16) = √144 = 12.
(12.5 is the arithmetic mean, not the mean proportional.) Answer: 12.

questions.text: The price of an article is first increased by 20% and then the new price is decreased by 20%. What is the net change in the price?
If A : B = 2 : 3 and B : C = 4 : 5, what is A : B : C?
questions.explanation:
Make the common term B equal. B is 3 in the first ratio and 4 in the second; LCM = 12.
A : B = 2 : 3 = 8 : 12 (multiply by 4). B : C = 4 : 5 = 12 : 15 (multiply by 3).
So A : B : C = 8 : 12 : 15. Answer: 8 : 12 : 15.

questions.text: A bag contains ₹1, 50-paise and 25-paise coins in the ratio 1 : 2 : 4 by number. If the total value of the coins is ₹360, how many 25-paise coins are there?
questions.explanation:
Let the numbers of coins be x, 2x and 4x.
Total value = x × ₹1 + 2x × ₹0.50 + 4x × ₹0.25 = x + x + x = ₹3x.
3x = 360, so x = 120.
Number of 25-paise coins = 4x = 480. Answer: 480.

questions.text: The average weight of 8 persons increases by 2.5 kg when a new person comes in place of one of them who weighs 65 kg. What is the weight of the new person?
questions.explanation:
Increase in total weight = 8 × 2.5 = 20 kg.
This whole increase comes from the new person replacing the 65 kg person.
New person's weight = 65 + 20 = 85 kg. Answer: 85 kg.

questions.text: A batsman has an average of 32 runs in 10 innings. How many runs must he score in the 11th innings to raise his average to 36?
questions.explanation:
Runs in 10 innings = 10 × 32 = 320.
Runs needed for an average of 36 in 11 innings = 11 × 36 = 396.
Required score = 396 − 320 = 76.
Shortcut: new average + (old innings × increase) = 36 + 10 × 4 = 76. Answer: 76.

questions.text: The population of a town is 20,000. It increases by 10% in the first year and by 5% in the second year. What is the population at the end of the second year?
questions.explanation:
After year 1: 20,000 × 110/100 = 22,000.
After year 2: 22,000 × 105/100 = 23,100.
(Adding 10% + 5% = 15% gives 23,000, which ignores growth on the increased population.) Answer: 23,100.

questions.text: In an election between two candidates, 10% of the votes cast were declared invalid. The winner got 55% of the valid votes and won by 1,800 votes. How many votes were cast in total?
questions.explanation:
Let total votes cast = V. Valid votes = 90% of V = 0.9V.
The winner gets 55% and the loser 45% of valid votes, so the margin is 10% of valid votes = 0.09V.
0.09V = 1,800, so V = 20,000.
(18,000 is the number of valid votes, not total votes cast.) Answer: 20,000.

questions.text: A man spends 75% of his income. His income increases by 20% and his expenditure increases by 10%. By what percent do his savings increase?
questions.explanation:
Take income = ₹100, so expenditure = ₹75 and savings = ₹25.
New income = ₹120; new expenditure = 75 × 1.10 = ₹82.50.
New savings = 120 − 82.50 = ₹37.50.
Increase = 12.50 on 25 = 50%. Answer: 50%.
